title: Hearing the Word
definition: Hearing the Word is the faithful receiving of Scripture as it is read, taught, preached, and applied among God's people.
summary: God calls His people not only to private reading but also to gather under the public ministry of the Word.
christFocus: Christ's sheep hear His voice, and the preached and read Word calls people to faith, repentance, worship, and endurance.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Hearing the Word teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to hearing the word by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
